title: Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Larry David, Timothée Chalamet, and More Watch New York Knicks' Miraculous Comeback in NBA Finals History
text:
A list of celebrities who attended the New York Knicks' historic comeback against the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals, including Spike Lee, Adam Sandler, Ben Stiller, Larry David, and Timothée Chalamet.
Spike Lee , Adam Sandler , Ben Stiller , Larry David , Timothée Chalamet and More Watch New York Knicks Pull Off Biggest Comeback in NBA Finals History ’24 Jump Street’ in the Works With Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum and Ice Cube in Talks to Return ‘Toy Story 5’ First Reactions Praise Pixar’s Sequel as a ‘Deeply Profound’ and ‘Moving’ Film That ‘Ranks Right Alongside’ the Original Tom Hanks Says Taylor Swift’s ‘Toy Story 5’ Song Was Kept ‘Top Secret’ From the Cast Until Release Day It was a who’s who on the sidelines of Madison Square Garden as the New York Knicks fronted a miraculous comeback against the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the NBA Finals.flew all the way from Tuesday night’s “Toy Story 5” premiere to watch MSG explode as the Knicks took a 3-1 lead over the Spurs.
Tom Hanks Says Taylor Swift's 'Toy Story 5' Song Was Kept 'Top Secret' From the Cast Until Release DayThe Knicks, down by 29 points, looked down and out heading into the fourth quarter. But with the support of the thundering MSG crowd, the Knicks managed to bring it within one with 1:47 to go.
After back-to-back missed free throws from Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, Knicks guard Jalen Brunson brought it down the other end and gave his team the first lead of the night with a clutch floater. Stephon Castle managed to give the Spurs a one-point lead after two free throws of his own, but the Knicks took it right back after a bucket from forward OG Anunoby with a little over a second to go.
Spurs were unable to convert on their final possession, and the Knicks had done it. The final score was 106 to 107. Wednesday’s game was the biggest comeback in NBA finals history, per “Inside the NBA. ” The show’s hosts were flabbergasted in their post-game coverage.
Analyst Ernie Johnson opened his commentary by asking his co-hosts, “What the hell did we just see? ” Charles Barkley was quick to fault the Spurs for allowing such an explosive Knicks’ comeback: “When you blow a 29-point lead, the other team has to help you.
